title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: In (b) the acyclicity condition is transcribed 'H^i(C^·)=0 si i ≥ 0'. It should be i>0 (equivalently i≠0, as on the previous page). Otherwise the resolution would resolve 0.

The two classes of functors are muddled on this page. Both are written Hom_{k,Σ-ex}, but the next page distinguishes Σ-sex (case a) from Σ-ex (case b). As written, (a) and (b) appear to use the same source category yet give different essential images. The intended correction is that (a) uses the larger class (Σ-sex) and (b) the class that also commutes with Σ-moyennes, or the reverse. Which assignment is right is not determinable from the page alone.

Full faithfulness in (a) implicitly needs Σ.-projectivity of the C^i. and the dévissage of objects of P.. These are only supplied on the next page as 'indications'. The fact that composites of Σ-monos are Σ-monos is flagged on the previous page as possibly needing to be imposed as an axiom; in Quillen's axioms it is built in.

ideas.what: Class Σ of short exact sequences in an additive category, with Σ-monos/epis, Σ-projectives, and Σ-strict morphisms factoring through a 'Σ-moyenne'
ideas.modern_name: Exact category (Quillen); admissible/strict morphisms and admissible image
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen 1973 (Higher algebraic K-theory I), also Heller 1958; strict morphisms, e.g., Bühler 2010 exposition
ideas.where_published: Relative homological algebra with a class of exact sequences goes back to Hochschild/Heller/Buchsbaum; Grothendieck's own use is unsure

ideas.what: Σ-special complexes and Σ-resolutions (complexes splitting into short Σ-sequences through Ker, Im, Coim, H)
ideas.modern_name: Acyclic complexes in an exact category / complexes with admissible differentials (Neeman, Keller, Bühler)

ideas.what: Universal exact k-category (P., Σ.) with a tautological complex C^·. built from disks C^i. and spheres Ψ^i.; Σ-exact functors out of P. correspond, fully faithfully, to complexes with admissible differentials, and the finer class to Σ-resolutions
ideas.modern_name: Free/classifying exact category for a complex or resolution; corepresentability of complexes by an exact category of perfect graded/complex objects (cf. universal properties of Ch^b(proj k), Dold–Kan style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard single credit; related ideas in Keller, Schlichting, and free stable ∞-category on one object (Lurie); unsure

ideas.what: Dévissage of objects of P. as iterated extensions of shifted copies of the unit along the stupid filtration (Gr_i L ≅ Ψ^i ⊗ L_i)
ideas.where_published: SGA 6 uses such filtrations for perfect complexes

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates (as 'il faudrait prouver') a corepresentability theorem: complexes with Σ-admissible differentials in any exact k-category B, and in particular Σ-resolutions, are classified by Σ-exact functors from a single model exact category P. of graded/complex objects. This 'universal exact category carrying a resolution' does not appear as such in the standard exact-category literature, which phrases such things via derived/∞-categorical universal properties instead.
missed.quote: est universel pour les triples (B, C^·; Σ) tels que les d^i: C^i → C^{i+1} aient des Σ-moyennes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives an exact-categorical (1-categorical, non-derived) universal property for resolutions. Such a statement is useful for defining natural invariants of resolutions (determinants, multiplicative structures, K-theory operations) once on a model. It parallels later universal-property results for stable ∞-categories and Waldhausen categories, but at the level of exact categories, where it seems less documented.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but unproved universal-property statement for exact categories carrying a resolution, aimed at the dévissage of perfect complexes. It anticipates the 'classifying object' philosophy later standard in ∞-categorical form. Exact categories themselves and the techniques are routine, and the result is plausible and elementary for a specialist, so the novelty is modest.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Il faudrait prouver' seems correct; the following line likely reads 'Soit B une cat. additive karoubienne, Σ une famille de suites exactes', with an interlinear alternative 'i.e. B cat. abélienne, Σ toutes les suites ex.'.
The interlinear phrase 'ou tensoflèches[?]' is doubtful; it probably reads 'ou suffisantes' or relates to 'Σ-moyennes'. Unreadable with confidence.
The bracketed note reading 'dans P(P., C^·.; Σ.)' is more plausibly '[donc (P., C^·., Σ.) est universel pour les triples (B, C^·, Σ)...'.
In b), 'H^i(C^·)=0 si i ≥ 0' should likely read 'si i > 0' (or 'i ≠ 0').
The functor-class subscript in (a) is probably 'Σ-sex', as on the next page; it is transcribed as 'Σ-ex' in both (a) and (b).
